extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, and statistical reasoning) and five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, and visual question answering) across diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.inLanguage: English (with 6.57% non-English questions including Chinese and Persian)
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024. arXiv:2310.02255v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected by: (1) collecting nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (2,666 examples); (2) reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and collecting 19 that contain math-related instances (2,739 examples after filtering and human labeling); and (3) creating three new datasets—IQTest (228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (400 examples on functional plots), and PaperQA (107 examples from academic paper figures released in August 2023 on Huggingface). Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples (5,261 out of 6,141) have annotations, as annotations were sourced from original data providers. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was sourced from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. Sources include geometry problem datasets (Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo), math word problem datasets (CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP), textbook QA datasets (SciBench, TheoremQA), VQA datasets (ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS), and newly annotated datasets (IQTest from online learning platforms, FunctionQA, PaperQA from Huggingface papers released in August 2023).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. Multimodal Bard evaluation dates range from Sep 8, 2023 to Sep 10, 2023. GPT-4V evaluation dates range from Oct 7, 2023 to Oct 15, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. The dataset was divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets using a sampling strategy: first randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset, then randomly sample remaining questions proportionally.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select math-related examples (numeric answers or quantity words in questions), yielding 4,949 candidates. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting to finalize 2,739 examples. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details, and verified by expert annotators on 1,000 examples (94.1% exact match). Examples are annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was used: each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers (achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate; only 6 out of 736 questions had disagreements), then discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For VQA dataset labeling, three expert annotators labeled whether problems involve mathematical reasoning using defined criteria. For mathematical reasoning category labeling, expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidates. Human performance baseline was established using Amazon Mechanical Turk with annotators required to have a high school diploma or higher, a history of more than 5,000 HIT tasks, and an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in paper figures). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance baseline and Multimodal Bard assessment task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling was measured using Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. For the three new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 questions had disagreements). For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation, 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitment to maintaining datasets (refining potential data noise in response to community feedback) and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models. testmini contains 1,000 examples for model development validation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes images of people (some questions involve identifying celebrities and their ages). Multimodal Bard was restricted from responding to images of people in some cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista aims to facilitate the development of AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery. The benchmark is intended to drive progress toward general-purpose AI assistants with strong mathematical reasoning in visual contexts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains like science and college-level math may limit generalizability. The dataset coverage may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations sourced from original data providers lack unified format and structure. The benchmark may not fully represent all types of mathematical problems and visual contexts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on specific domains necessitates a more labor-intensive collection process, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous sources. The benchmark focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models given rapid development in foundation models. Non-English questions (6.57%) require multilingual model capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) in visual contexts. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test subset (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation. The benchmark supports fine-grained evaluation across mathematical reasoning types, visual context types, task categories, and grade levels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 5 human annotators per question for the human performance baseline on testmini. 3 expert annotators for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling and for the three new datasets.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human performance baseline annotators: required high school diploma or higher, history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks, acceptance score higher than 0.99. New dataset annotators: graduate students in STEM fields. VQA mathematical reasoning labelers: expert annotators (3 per example).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used as answer extractor with >99.5% accuracy on 200 examples), EasyOCR (for OCR text detection), Multimodal Bard (for image caption generation in augmented LLM experiments).
